children: By Alexander Ward and Lara Seligman

WASHINGTON — President Trump called Elon Musk on Wednesday and asked him to lift restrictions on a military-grade version of Starlink in Ukraine that the SpaceX chief had throttled, U.S. officials said.

Some U.S. and Ukrainian officials said the system was working more normally on Thursday, after Trump and Musk spoke, but wasn't restored to full functionality. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Friday "the speed has not been restored."
"I've heard it was fixed but if it's not I'll speak to him," Trump told reporters Friday, referring to Musk.

Trump told Musk in their Wednesday call that he was frustrated the system's speeds remained capped at around 100 miles an hour, officials said. The speed limit rendered some of Ukraine's offensive drones and interceptors powerless against Russian attacks. Their conversation followed a Wall Street Journal report revealing that Musk ordered the slowdown, though SpaceX and the White House have differing accounts about whether the world's richest man acted alone or at the administration's behest.
Trump has told aides and allies this week that he wanted to reverse the slowdown of Starlink, which Ukraine's forces use to defend themselves along the front line, the officials said.

"Removal of the throttle limit will do much to enable Ukraine's strike capabilities at operational depths and its current effort to scale up deployment of jet-powered interceptors," said Michael Kofman, an expert on the war at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace. Kofman added that he had heard from Ukrainian military units that early tests suggest the system is now working more regularly.
"I don't comment one way or the other," Trump said on Thursday when asked about the Journal's reporting that he had called Musk. "The bottom line: He put it back."
On Friday, Trump called Musk "a very good person" and said he would "never do anything wrong."
"I know him very well, he's a fair person and you know it's an unusual situation where they're talking to a private company. But he's not going to do anything that's wrong," Trump said.

Some Ukrainian units had successfully tested drones at 200 kilometers, or 125 miles, an hour on Thursday, raising hopes that normal service was being resumed after over a week of severe disruptions. But as of Friday, most of Ukraine's military was still reporting failing connections at higher speeds, military and government officials said.
"We keep waiting for the information and clarification from the American side about the situation. There is no response yet," a Ukrainian official said.
Musk and SpaceX didn't respond to requests for comment.

The White House referred the Journal to Trump's recent denials that he had asked Musk to throttle Starlink's speeds or knew who issued the order. Trump and Musk spoke about Ukraine and Starlink on the day the slowdown became public, the Journal previously reported.

The president and his top officials have spent a week facing questions about why Starlink was throttled and whether they ordered it. The slowdown began days after Trump and Musk both publicly criticized Zelensky for attacking Russian diesel refineries, which Trump blames for elevated energy prices. Trump has repeatedly denied giving the order or knowing who did.
The connectivity issues helped sink U.S.-Ukraine relations to their lowest level in months.

Asked about Musk's decision to throttle Starlink, Vice President JD Vance on Thursday told reporters that "it's completely understandable that he doesn't want to get in the middle of a war without the U.S. government effectively directing him on what to do."
"I don't think this is about Elon. I think it's fundamentally about what America's policy in Ukraine and Russia is going to be," he said.

His message differed from comments by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio that Musk had the authority to enforce his company's terms of service without input from the administration.
"There are terms of service that ultimately need to be complied to, and that's where Starlink has the option to make those decisions," Hegseth said, speaking to reporters earlier this week.

The speed cap meant Ukrainian hardware couldn't stay connected to the satellite-based network when traveling at high rates of speed, according to people familiar with the matter. Ukrainian officials said the move would cost Ukrainian lives.
Russia overnight launched another massive barrage against Kyiv, Ukraine's capital, just a day after Moscow said it had agreed to trilateral talks with the U.S. and Ukraine to end the war.

Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D., Conn.) on Thursday announced an investigation into how Starlink was degraded for Ukraine without notice and the implications of the Pentagon's dependence on SpaceX for critical satellite communications.
